rationale: Retain Hawaiʻi Gas as an active Argo-managed infrastructure investment and retain APG as a beneficial co-investor. Hawaiʻi Gas's July 2022 closing announcement confirms that ownership transferred to an Argo affiliate after Hawaiʻi PUC approval, and its June 2025 announcement states that Hawaiʻi Gas remains wholly owned by funds managed by Argo. APG's own 2022 SFDR disclosure lists Hawaiʻi Gas as an investment of APG Infrastructure Pool 2020-2021, while the acquisition materials filed with the SEC identify APG and CalSTRS as committed-capital investors. No later Argo or APG disposition, pending sale, or change of control was found through August 8, 2026. Correct APG's vague vehicle label to the disclosed APG Infrastructure Pool 2020-2021, add the legal AMF vehicle suffix for Argo, add the official website, refresh the concise operating description, replace the duplicate July 2022 milestone with the June 2022 regulatory approval, and attach direct evidence to every milestone. CalSTRS is not added in this manager-scoped task because it is outside the supplied 100-manager census and public materials reviewed do not disclose a separate current ownership period or stake for it.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Hawaiʻi Gas is the only government-franchised full-service gas utility in Hawaiʻi and a statewide propane distributor. Founded in 1904, it manufactures and distributes synthetic and renewable natural gas to utility customers on Oʻahu and supplies liquefied petroleum gas to residential and commercial customers across the state's six primary islands. Its operating base includes approximately 1,100 miles of pipeline, bulk storage, and delivery fleets. The company is wholly owned by funds managed by Argo through AMF Hawaiʻi Investment Holdings, LLC; APG Infrastructure Pool 2020-2021 disclosed Hawaiʻi Gas as an infrastructure investment following the July 2022 acquisition.

set.event: Honolulu Gas Company, the predecessor of Hawaiʻi Gas, was founded.
Hawaiʻi Gas announced that Argo Infrastructure Partners would acquire the company from Macquarie Infrastructure Corporation, subject to regulatory approval.
The Hawaiʻi Public Utilities Commission approved the transfer of control to AMF Hawaii Holdings, LLC in Decision and Order No. 38478.
Argo Infrastructure Partners completed its acquisition of Hawaiʻi Gas through an affiliated investment vehicle backed by institutional capital including APG.
Isle Gas, another wholly owned AMF subsidiary serviced by Hawaiʻi Gas, completed its acquisition of AmeriGas's Hawaiʻi propane storage and delivery assets.
